supergroups.other: Outside condensed matter, materials and quantum research

categories.name: Quantum algorithms, circuits and software
categories.definition: Research on constructing, optimizing, simulating, verifying or maintaining quantum algorithms, executable circuits and quantum programming systems.
categories.test: Choose when the domain result is a program, circuit, compiler or algorithm implementation judged by quantum semantics, resource counts or software correctness; ideal circuit simulations and execution on a QPU remain here unless device physics determines the result.
examples: QEDIA: Quantum Program Verification in Lean
Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
QASM-Eval: A Dataset to Train and Evaluate LLMs on OpenQASM-3 Beyond Quantum Circuits

categories.name: Quantum information theory and error-correcting codes
categories.definition: Research on quantum information resources, communication, cryptographic security, abstract error-correcting codes and mathematical limits of quantum computation.
categories.test: Choose when the main claim concerns entropies, entanglement as an information resource, Bell correlations, channel capacities, code parameters, security or quantum computational complexity rather than implementing a particular program or studying a material phase.
examples: Large-Language-Model Discovery of Quantum LDPC Codes through Structured Concept Evolution
Sharp continuity of quantum conditional entropy
Private communication via zero-private-capacity quantum channels

categories.name: Quantum devices, control and infrastructure
categories.definition: Research on physical qubit and quantum-sensing platforms, device calibration and control, quantum-network links and their enabling cryogenic or laboratory infrastructure.
categories.test: Choose when judging the result requires physical device expertise, such as qubit operating points, pulse dynamics, coherence, calibration signals, ion transport, link-generation probabilities or dilution cooling; a physics-grounded simulation can qualify.
examples: zenDot: An LLM-integrated quantum TCAD platform for semiconductor quantum-device design and optimization automation
Onnes: A Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Simulator for Cryogenic Fault Diagnosis in Quantum Computing Infrastructure
Vibe Calibration: Autonomous Bring-up of a 112-Qubit Superconducting Quantum Processor by a Skill-Orchestrating Language Agent

categories.name: Metals, alloys and engineering materials
categories.definition: Research restricted to metals, alloys, metallic glasses, high-entropy solids or engineered load-bearing and irradiation-resistant materials, including composites, cement and refractory compound families.
categories.test: Choose for class-specific composition, processing, corrosion, deformation, fracture, durability or performance studies and knowledge resources; named metallic hosts belong here unless a dominant catalytic, battery, electronic or collective quantum property sets another material field.
examples: LLM-guided phase diagram construction through high-throughput experimentation
CP-Agent: A Harness-Engineered Agent for Crystal Plasticity Simulation Workflows
Applications of bio-enhanced cementitious composites for sustainable building materials: emission-reduction and carbon-sequestration pathways

categories.name: Polymers, molecular materials and soft matter
categories.definition: Research on polymers and resins, non-framework molecular solids and energetic compounds, colloids, jamming and active particulate matter.
categories.test: Choose when the abstract is restricted to these systems and requires expertise in molecular organization, polymer architecture, thermal transitions, soft mechanics or particulate statistical physics, including class-specific tools and benchmarks.
examples: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics of Polymers
Thermal pathway reconstruction exposes a reliability gap for AI-guided materials design
Scale-free correlations in extremely persistent active matter

categories.name: Porous frameworks and adsorbing layered hosts
categories.definition: Research on metal-organic and covalent organic frameworks, responsive porous crystals and layered adsorbent hosts whose synthesis, pore structure or guest-host behavior is the subject.
categories.test: Choose for framework-specific synthesis, validation, screening, adsorption, separation or guest-induced transitions, and for composition-dependent hydration of layered hosts; an electrode or catalysis objective takes precedence over the host label.
examples: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
Large Language Model-Assisted Systematic Study of Anomalous Adsorption Phenomena
Agent-MD: Selective LLM Intervention with Event-Driven Escalation for Stateful GCMC--MD Campaigns

categories.name: Battery materials, catalysts and reactive surfaces
categories.definition: Research on battery electrodes, electrolytes and interphases, catalytic materials and surface-adsorbate systems whose ionic, electrochemical or reactive behavior defines the study.
categories.test: Choose for studies restricted to battery materials or catalysts, including their synthesis, curation and characterization, or for substantive adsorption-energy and reaction-mechanism results on catalytic surfaces; a generic structure-building demonstration alone does not qualify.
examples: Graph neural networks and machine learning interatomic potentials for voltage prediction and screening high energy density sodium-ion cathode materials
Accelerating battery materials discovery with an agentic AI for automated XPS analysis integrating physical constraints and chemometrics
Autonomous heterogeneous catalyst discovery with a self-evolving multi-agent digital twin

categories.name: Electronic, optical and inorganic functional materials
categories.definition: Research on semiconductors, classical electronic and photonic devices, optical and dielectric materials, thermoelectrics and specified inorganic functional compound families such as oxide perovskites and elpasolites.
categories.test: Choose for class-restricted electronic, optical, dielectric, thermoelectric or functional-compound studies and resources, including perovskite-family structure or synthesis studies; unrestricted inorganic-crystal prediction and generation belong to a methods community even if band gap is an objective.
examples: PervoTransformer: Multi-Scale Transformer-Based Device Design and Atomistic Modeling of Perovskites
Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
From High-Throughput Screening to Generative Design: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Dielectric Materials Discovery

categories.name: Magnetism, correlated matter and many-body condensed-matter theory
categories.definition: Research on magnetic, superconducting, topological and correlated matter and the spin, lattice and many-body models used to understand its phases, spectra and dynamics.
categories.test: Choose when the physics result concerns collective material behavior, phase identification, magnetic response, superconductivity, localization, integrable spin systems or many-body spectral and topological properties; proofs about these systems qualify without a named chemical compound.
examples: Grounded autonomous research: a fault-tolerant LLM pipeline from corpus to manuscript in frontier computational physics
Bethe Ansatz with a Large Language Model
Improving the lower bound on the Laughlin gap: An SDP search

categories.name: Electronic structure and atomistic simulation
categories.definition: Research on transferable electronic-structure, quantum-chemical and atomistic modeling methods and workflows, including DFT, many-body electronic structure, interatomic potentials, molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo.
categories.test: After checking material-class precedence, choose when the central domain expertise is building simulation-ready atomistic models, selecting physical approximations, configuring or executing calculations, converging solvers, developing potentials or validating physical simulation workflows.
examples: AutoDFT: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous DFT Calculations
MASON: Materials Atomistic Structure builder Operated in Natural language
GROMACS-Agent: Text-to-Workflow Generation for Molecular Dynamics A multi-agent framework for topology-aware GROMACS workflow generation, evaluation, correction, and selected safe execution

categories.name: Diffraction, crystallography, spectroscopy and metrology
categories.definition: Research on transferable structure determination and quantitative materials analysis from diffraction, spectra and related non-imaging physical measurements.
categories.test: After checking material-class precedence, choose when the domain content concerns indexing, phase identification, refinement, measurement-based structural inference, spectral interpretation or quantitative probe-response analysis such as thermoreflectance, rather than generic crystal generation or spatial imaging.
examples: NeuDiff Agent: a governed AI workflow for single-crystal neutron crystallography
AutoXRD: Autonomous LLM Agents and Comprehensive Evaluation for Powder Diffraction Analysis
RamanGPT: Bidirectional Mapping Between Crystal Structures and Raman Spectra with Graph Neural Networks and Generative Transformers

categories.name: Microscopy and spatially resolved characterization
categories.definition: Research on transferable electron, X-ray and scanning-probe microscopy, image-based materials characterization and associated instrument control or specimen preparation.
categories.test: After checking material-class precedence, choose when the abstract centers on acquiring or interpreting spatial images, image-derived microstructure, tip or beam conditioning, tomography, microscope-local spectroscopy or FIB milling across materials.
examples: STEMGym: Benchmarking Sequential Decision-Making under Dose Budgets in Autonomous Electron Microscopy
Unmodeled states and uncertain action outcomes in agentic scanning tunneling microscopy
TEM Agent: enhancing transmission electron microscopy with modern AI tools

categories.name: Synthesis planning and laboratory automation
categories.definition: Research on transferable synthesis chemistry, process planning and experimental laboratory orchestration across material classes.
categories.test: After checking material-class precedence, choose when the domain result concerns viable synthesis routes, precursors, reaction conditions, deposition or mixing protocols, robotic execution or integration of an experimental laboratory; use the appropriate measurement community for a specific analytical instrument.
examples: ProvMind: Provenance-grounded reasoning for materials synthesis
Evaluating LLM-based AI agents integrated with materials synthesis tools: the case of atomic layer deposition
NIMO Controller: a self-driving laboratory orchestrator based on the Model Context Protocol

categories.name: Materials informatics and data-driven discovery
categories.definition: Research on transferable materials-data representations, databases, ontologies, learned property models, generative crystal design and statistical search or optimization over materials candidates.
categories.test: After checking material-class precedence, choose when the scientific object is a materials dataset, representation, database comparison, statistical predictor, candidate generator or acquisition policy rather than the physical validity or execution of a simulation or experiment.
examples: MatQuery: Execution-Grounded Natural-Language Querying over Heterogeneous Materials Databases
Optimizing Expert-Designed Crystal Graph Networks for Band-Gap Prediction with an Autonomous LLM Research Loop
Portfolio-Based Constrained Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Materials Design

categories.name: Materials science across communities
categories.definition: Reviews, perspectives and knowledge or reasoning studies spanning materials science as a whole without a dominant material or technique community.
categories.test: Use only when the abstract substantively spans several material classes and several methods communities, and no one specialist community accounts for its central scope; tools, database methods, synthesis reviews and simulation benchmarks must instead receive their specific methods field.
examples: Large language models in materials science: mechanistic understanding, structure–property reasoning and future opportunities
MatSciBench: Benchmarking the Reasoning Ability of Large Language Models in Materials Science
OmniMatBench: A Human-Calibrated Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark Across 19 Materials Science Subfields

categories.name: Outside condensed matter, materials and quantum research
categories.definition: Papers whose physics, chemistry or other scientific content belongs to a community outside condensed matter, materials science and quantum computing or information: molecular and quantum chemistry, biology and medicine, other areas of physics, mathematics, economics or general scientific methods without a materials or quantum focus.
categories.test: Choose when none of the other categories' communities would be the natural referee for the scientific content, for example molecular quantum chemistry, biological microscopy, radiation transport, pure mathematics or a general-purpose scientific agent evaluated without a materials or quantum focus. Do not choose it merely because the AI method is general.
examples: Can Autonomous LLM Agents Execute Multireference Quantum Chemistry Calculations?
Million-scale multimodal pollen microscopy with expert-guided foundation models
TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving

tie_breaking: Assign exactly one FIELD by the expertise needed to judge the physics or materials content of the main results, or the sustained content of a review or benchmark; AI architecture, model size, agent count, code generation, question answering and extraction are not field criteria.

Material-class precedence: choose a material category when the evidence and evaluation are restricted to that class or when the paper reports a substantive result about it; otherwise choose the technique community whose physical or materials methods are being developed or evaluated. A named illustrative material does not establish the field.

Operationalize restriction using the evaluated scope, required domain assumptions and scientific conclusions rather than whether the authors call their method generalizable: a polymer-only benchmark, MOF validation resource or alloy-only database stays with its material community even if the extraction or optimization algorithm could transfer.

Distinguish a substantive material result from a tool demonstration: a composition-dependent trend, measured property improvement, phase discovery or physically interpreted mechanism sets a material field; successful execution, numerical reproduction, schema fidelity or runtime savings on a convenient example normally leaves a transferable method in its methods community. If the entire study and its domain assumptions are class-specific, the restriction itself suffices.

For multiple material systems, use their shared category if one covers all substantive studies, otherwise a clearly dominant class; absent either, use the dominant methods community. Use cross-materials only for work genuinely spanning materials science as a whole, never merely because a technique works on several chemistries.

Materials informatics versus atomistic simulation: learned structure-property regression, descriptors, database search, inverse crystal generation and Bayesian acquisition policies are materials-informatics; choosing electronic-structure theory, building simulation-ready geometries, validating forces or potentials, and setting up or executing DFT, MD or Monte Carlo are atomistic-simulation. Judge what must be physically validated, not whether structures or DFT-labelled data appear.

A generative crystal model trained on Materials Project with SUN or property-prediction metrics belongs to materials-informatics, even if DFT relaxation is its evaluator; a geometry builder for slabs, defects and interfaces or a tool for simulator configuration belongs to atomistic-simulation. A model inferred from measured diffraction belongs to diffraction-spectroscopy.

A machine-learning interatomic potential is atomistic-simulation when forces, energies, trajectories or simulation stability are the object; embedding an existing potential inside a general property-prediction representation does not by itself move materials-informatics to atomistic-simulation. Class-restricted potential development still follows the material class.

Materials informatics versus synthesis-labs: prediction or optimization over generic candidate/property tables belongs to materials-informatics, including offline Bayesian-optimization studies motivated by self-driving labs; chemically valid routes, precursors, reaction conditions and physical laboratory execution belong to synthesis-labs. A synthesis-knowledge benchmark follows synthesis-labs, not cross-materials.

Generic literature digitization, materials ontologies, knowledge graphs and database construction belong to materials-informatics because their community concerns reusable materials evidence and data representations; a class-restricted resource belongs to its material category, and an extraction study centered on reproducing physical simulation workflows can belong to atomistic-simulation.

Diffraction-spectroscopy versus microscopy: indexing, phase identification and structure refinement from diffraction belong to diffraction-spectroscopy; spatial image formation, reconstruction, segmentation, tip conditioning and instrument-local analytical imaging belong to microscopy. Electron diffraction, EBSD and EELS embedded in an electron-microscope workflow follow microscopy when imaging and acquisition dominate; standalone reciprocal-space structure refinement follows diffraction-spectroscopy.

Raman analysis, non-imaging XPS and thermoreflectance fall within diffraction-spectroscopy when transferable probe physics and quantitative analysis are central. Battery-SEI XPS, ferroelectric-domain switching or magnetic spin-wave spectroscopy follow their material communities when restricted to those systems or reporting their physics; the presence of a particular instrument is not overriding.

Generic fracture-surface image recognition belongs to microscopy and transferable crystallographic plane inference belongs to diffraction-spectroscopy; reinforced fracture architectures, concrete and irradiation-resistant engineering solids belong to structural-materials. Do not infer an alloy solely from automotive processing language.

Quantum software versus quantum information: executable circuit construction, program verification, SDK maintenance and gate-level resource optimization belong to quantum-software; code distance or rate, channel capacity, cryptographic security, information inequalities and query-complexity or completeness theorems belong to quantum-information. Formalization in Lean decides neither.

Error-correcting-code discovery belongs to quantum-information when the main object is a code family or encoding and its distance, rate or abstract noise performance; implemented syndrome-extraction or decoding circuit design belongs to quantum-software. A code/circuit co-design paper without a dominant code-theoretic result follows quantum-software; quantum-hardware requires substantive platform physics beyond a generic error model or qubit budget.

Quantum hardware requires device-specific parameters or substantive physical constraints: qubit and defect coherence, calibration plots, pulse dynamics, cryogenic faults, ion transport and stochastic link generation qualify, even in simulation. Circuit-level topology constraints, hardware-facing programming syntax or a demonstration on IBM/IonQ do not alone override quantum-software.

Quantum control follows quantum-hardware when continuous-time dynamics, physical pulse limits, noise or platform-constrained protocols determine the result; abstract ansatz or variational circuit optimization follows quantum-software. Ideal CHSH circuit implementations remain quantum-software; fundamental Bell bounds belong to quantum-information.

The quantum supergroup is for computing and information, not every quantum-mechanical system: spin-chain solvability, spin-glass limits, Laughlin gaps, topological edge spectra, many-body operator-entanglement growth and matrix-product-state phase theorems belong to quantum-matter when they concern condensed-matter models. Computational-complexity theorems about a Hubbard energy problem belong to quantum-information; quantum-walk localization without an algorithmic claim follows quantum-matter.

Superconducting transition temperatures, permanent magnets, altermagnetism and superconducting-state selection belong to quantum-matter; superconducting-qubit calibration and sensing-defect coherence belong to quantum-hardware. Classical transistor and optical-device studies follow electronic-functional, including non-qubit semiconductor quantum dots.

Preserve the SUBJECT functional priorities inside the material groups: electrodes, electrolytes and battery interphases or catalytic function override alloy, polymer, semiconductor or porous-framework chemistry and go to energy-reactive; organic semiconductors and emitters go to electronic-functional, not molecular-soft.

Porous-hosts includes MOFs, COFs, soft porous crystals and layered clay hosts when adsorption, hydration or guest-host structure is substantive; framework synthesis and ZnO-to-ZIF-8 conversion follow the framework product. A framework studied as an electrode or catalyst goes to energy-reactive.

Electronic-functional merges the former semiconductor-optical and most functional-solids families: perovskite solar cells, semiconductor halides, organic electronics, optical multilayers, dielectric polymers and crystals, thermoelectric chalcogenides, oxide/double-perovskite and elpasolite family studies qualify; a band-gap target across unrestricted inorganic crystals does not.

Structural-materials includes metallic glasses, high-entropy solids, composites, construction/reactor materials and MAX-phase engineering ceramics. A balanced refractory/soft-magnetic alloy study keeps this shared alloy category, while a permanent-magnet-only study goes to quantum-matter; corrosion of specified metal hosts stays structural-materials, whereas inhibitor molecules without a specified host merge into molecular-soft.

For vague or missing abstracts, use only the supplied title and tags and flag the decision as provisional; do not invent chemistry, physical function or community from an AI label. Prefer a positively supported methods community over cross-materials, which is not a missing-information category; if no dominant community can be established, record uncertainty for adjudication.

notes.axis: FIELD: the research community whose expertise is needed to judge the physics or materials content of a paper
notes.origin: Built by GPT-6.1 Sol agents from the titles and abstracts of an earlier, broader candidate set of papers on language models in condensed matter, materials and quantum research; the category other-fields was added for the reviewed papers outside these fields.
